newsitem.title: UK: U.S. actor berates archbishop over smacking.
newsitem.headline: U.S. actor berates archbishop over smacking.

text.p: Woody Harrelson, American star of the serial killer film "Natural Born Killers," on Monday berated Britain's Archbishop of Canterbury for saying it was acceptable to discipline children with a "gentle slap."

George Carey, leader of the Anglican church, sparked controversy last week when he said there was nothing wrong with administering children a gentle slap "as long as it is done with love and with firm discipline within the family set-up".
That prompted Harrelson to write a tongue-in-cheek letter to the London Independent newspaper from Los Angeles.
"I was wondering, now that my oldest daughter is nearly four-years-old and gaining strength, how long I have to wait before I can start slapping my new-born.
"Should I wait until she is out of her infancy, or should I get started while she is still in the crib?"
Harrelson rose to fame as the dumb barman in the U.S. television comedy series "Cheers" before taking the starring role in Oliver Stone's "Natural Born Killers."
The film, with its graphic depictions of nearly 100 murders, was linked with a string of copycat killings abroad after its release in 1994.
